title: Optimize Console: Action Streamline, Temporal Diff Stream, and Forensic Apply Chronicle
creator: Aisha Park
description: Summary: Build a compact, action-oriented Optimize Console surface that presents batching & caching recommendations as bite-sized action cards, shows an inline temporal diff stream for previewing combined config changes, and records a searchable forensic apply chronicle (audit trail) to support safe applies and automated rollback. Background: Customers run many models with variable seq lengths and exhibit noisy suggestion sets; they need an approachable interface to accept batching/caching suggestions without risking regressions. This ticket scopes the UX and acceptance criteria for the product and coordinates design + engineering work. Goals: 1) Reduce time-to-accept by 40% for non-expert users accepting safe recommendations. 2) Surface per-change cost delta, expected P95 latency delta, and estimated risk score. 3) Provide an immutable apply chronicle that links to runtime snapshots and a one-click rewind/rollback sandbox. Out of scope: server-side kernel selection logic, deep model quantization recommendations (handled by Optimize engine), and billing contract changes.
acceptance_criteria: Compact action cards show: title, short rationale, estimated monthly savings (USD), estimated latency impact (P50/P95), confidence score, and quick-apply button.
Temporal diff stream displays combined diffs across selected cards with highlighted token-level cost deltas and an expandable per-route preview.
Apply chronicle records: timestamp, user id, diff snapshot id, runtime snapshot id, pre-apply simulation result, canary rollout config, and automated checksum for integrity.
Rollback flow allows operator to trigger a simulated rewind (dry-run) and then a staged rollback with canary traffic and health gating.
Telemetry: track accept/reject rate, mean time to accept, rollback frequency, and false-positive incidents toggled as regressions within 7 days.
Design QA: mobile responsive card grid and compact list mode implemented for consoles with narrow width.
Security: apply chronicle stored in auditable store with access-level controls; logs redact PII.
engineering_notes: Eng must expose a diff-aggregation API that can materialize combined config snapshots for preview and for the chronicle store (ENG-40812).
Backend should return estimated savings and latency deltas computed by Optimize engine; UI will display and sort by confidence score.
Apply operation will create immutable snapshot objects: diffSnapshotId and runtimeSnapshotId. These IDs must be included in the chronicle event payload.
We will reuse existing RBAC checks for apply and introduce a feature-flag gated event integrity checksum to validate chronicle entries.
Performance: card grid must lazy-load cards and defer detailed cost breakdown until expanded to avoid adding >200ms render latency on first load.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal dogfooding (redwood-internal tenants) for 2 weeks behind feature flag. Phase 2: Beta customers (opt-in) with telemetry monitoring for 4 weeks. Phase 3: Gradual ramp to all customers with opt-out for legacy recommendation flow. Feature flags: optimize_console_v2_cards, optimize_temporal_diff, optimize_forensic_chronicle.
testing_plan: Unit tests for diff aggregation and chronicle write/read semantics.
E2E test: create suggestion set -> preview temporal diff -> apply -> verify chronicle entry and runtime snapshot linkage.
Simulated regression test: introduce a synthetic workload to validate canary gating blocks rollout when P95 latency increases beyond configured threshold.
UX acceptance: run moderated usability test with 8 PM/SE customers to validate card clarity and comprehension of cost/latency trade-offs.
open_questions: What is the canonical schema for the forensic chronicle event? (need ENG + Security alignment)
Should the temporal diff stream show merged changes as a single combined delta or keep per-card provenance visible by default?
How will billing calc reflect per-token savings shown in the UI vs actual invoice? Add hover help linking to billing docs.
What retention policy for chronicle entries (90 days vs 365 days)? Legal has requested 365 days for enterprise customers.
decisions: Use combined merged-diff view by default but provide a ‘show provenance’ toggle to expand per-card origin.
Chronicle events will be stored for 365 days for enterprise plans and 90 days for self-serve tiers.
Implement canary rollout and automated health gates (latency regressions) before completing a full apply.
Surface cost estimates in USD and percentage delta; include a confidence band from Optimize model.
